natural_report: Player slows with four enemies; enemies appear normal; three or fewer enemies play acceptably.

source_facts.player: main_game_tick_normal consumes PLAYER_TICK_PENDING; main_alive arms it after an even FB_SIM_SEQ completed epoch, unless PICKUP_TIMER holds it.
source_facts.enemy: enemy_tick_impl et_find_movement admits movement when LAST_FRAME hardware VBlank parity is even, subject to normal death/freeze/direction conditions.
source_facts.publication: framebuffer_irq_impl increments FRAMES at every VBlank and FB_SIM_SEQ only when a pending completed image publishes.
source_facts.step: Ordinary player and enemy motion both advance one packed byte horizontally or 320 framebuffer bytes vertically: two pixels.

3.clock_meaning: VBlank counter at each dispatch; intervals are between consecutive sampled dispatches, not movement-call or distance measurements.

interpretation: Confirmed source clock inconsistency plus observed even-parity aliasing supports the reported relative slowdown. With two VBlanks per committed image, player cadence can halve while even-phase enemy movement remains admitted every dispatch. Not a direct moving-player displacement measurement. Opposite hardware parity could suppress enemy movement instead.
reassessment: Leading explanation now includes movement scheduling as well as renderer cost. High-risk remains; no production change approved. Existing frozen-epoch policy and 27000 target remain. Synchronizing enemy parity alone would not restore player wall-clock pace or meet the frame target.
next_discriminating_probe: Reuse existing monitor harness on identified cold artifact; count actual player_tick and enemy movement entries, completed epochs, hardware VBlanks and actor displacement over short three/four-enemy straight-motion windows without pickup/gate/death/freeze interruptions. Each phase <=45 seconds; success requires named calls plus valid motion and byte/mapping identity; absent or interrupted window fails. Include opposite VBlank parity if designing a scheduling fix.
